footnotes: Banks have no cost of sales; the flow chart shows revenue (net interest income + noninterest income) going to noninterest expense and the provision for credit losses, leaving pre-tax income. Other items, net are the gains and charges the income statement shows outside these lines (−$26.2M in 2025). Efficiency ratio = noninterest expense ÷ revenue (lower is better).
Figures are from the company's Form 10-K for fiscal years ended Dec 31, 2025 and a year earlier, as filed with the SEC. Never estimated: items the filing does not report are left out.
Percentages are of revenue; figures may not sum due to rounding.

summary: Revenue (net interest income plus noninterest income) fell 1.2% to $723M in 2025. Net interest income rose 36.4% to $829M and noninterest income was −$106M, versus $124M; noninterest expense rose 17.4%, and the provision for credit losses was $0, versus $0.
Net income fell 26.2% to $88.2M, or $0.43 per diluted share, and the efficiency ratio was 82.6% versus 69.5%. Eastern Bankshares returned $212M through dividends and buybacks.
sources: Eastern Bankshares, Inc. Form 10-K for FY2025 (SEC EDGAR)
